annotations.text:
Capture is a photo, a location tag and high/low — plus one optional line if there is something a photo can't say.

Three taps and no keyboard in the common case. There is no title: a photo of a broken toilet seat says what a title would, and requiring one put a keyboard between someone and the thing in front of them.

The tags are seeded per household, so they are full on the day the app is installed — which is the day someone decides whether this is quicker than saying it out loud.

The screen a filtered list can't be.

Bounded by time available rather than importance; grouped by room because that is how work is batched; needs-parts pulled to the top, because one trip to the shop clears a fortnight of small jobs.

Triage — effort, needs-parts, due date, repeat, who's doing it. Priority is here too, but it was already set at capture.

Every control writes on tap. There is no Save button: triage is a series of small independent decisions, and confirming each one turns sorting twelve items into forty taps.

Direction B — Ink

Same system, charcoal instead of Fern for the primary. More conventionally professional, and it lets the photographs carry the only colour in the chrome.

The tradeoff: it gives up the warmth in the chrome that the brief asked for, and a household tool has no logo to carry an identity instead.
